H&P – Detailed

Consult Summary:
30-year-old non-smoking engineer with childhood asthma presents with 2–3 days of wheeze, exertional dyspnea, cough, and low-grade fever concerning for an acute asthma flare; salbutamol use advised to increase, spacer and peak-flow meter prescribed, antihistamine recommended, and telephone review arranged in one week.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Wheezy and “short of breath,” onset 2–3 days ago.  
• Course: Symptoms persist; unable to walk to work; occasionally struggles to finish sentences. No nocturnal breathlessness.  
• Associated symptoms: Frequent dry cough, subjective fever (self-checked 37 °C). No chest pain, no sputum, no hemoptysis.  
• Triggers/relievers: Possible pollen exposure; no specific trigger identified. No peak-flow monitoring in place.  
• Functional impact: Cannot exercise; working from home or on sick leave.  
• Review of systems: Denies chest pain, nocturnal symptoms, phlegm, hemoptysis; otherwise not discussed.

Past Medical History:
• Asthma – childhood onset, reportedly severe; required salbutamol inhaler and occasional hospital visits, never ICU. Last regular controller therapy stopped ≈3–4 years ago; intermittent salbutamol use since.  
• Hay fever (allergic rhinitis).  
• Eczema.  
No other chronic conditions reported.

Medications:
• Salbutamol inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented; currently used every few weeks and with exercise; instructed to increase to 2–4 puffs Q4H PRN.  
No other regular medications.

Allergies:
• No known drug allergies.

Social History:
• Lives with partner.  
• Occupation: Engineer; typically walks to work but currently working from home/sick leave.  
• Tobacco: Never smoker.  
• Alcohol: ~1 glass of wine every 2–3 days.  
• Recreational drugs: Not mentioned.

Family History:
• Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
(Not performed – telemedicine)  
Patient-reported temperature: 37 °C.

Investigations:
• None today. Plan to obtain home peak-flow readings (AM/PM for 1 week).

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Acute asthma exacerbation
  • Likely triggered by viral infection or allergens (pollen).  
  • Plan:  
    – Increase salbutamol 2–4 puffs via spacer every 4 hours PRN.  
    – Prescribe spacer; pharmacist to demonstrate correct technique.  
    – Prescribe peak-flow meter; instruct twice-daily recordings for 1 week.  
    – Arrange telephone review in 1 week to assess symptoms and peak-flow diary; consider maintenance therapy if indicated.  
    – Return/call sooner if temperature rises, wheeze worsens, unable to speak in sentences, night-time wakening, or any concern.

Issue 2: Allergic rhinitis (hay fever)
  • Plan: Start regular oral antihistamine (OTC; specific agent per pharmacist advice).

General Plan Items:
  • Educate on asthma action plan and inhaler technique at pharmacy.  
  • Safety-net: seek urgent care/ED if severe breathlessness, chest tightness, or no relief after salbutamol.

Quality checks:

Missing but clinically expected elements:
• Full vitals (HR, RR, BP, O2 sat).  
• Detailed inhaler regimen and adherence.  
• Immunization history (e.g., influenza, pneumococcal).  
• Family history of atopy/asthma.  
• Objective lung exam findings.

Internal conflicts:
• None noted.

Transcript quality:
• Clear; minor repetitions but clinically adequate.
